text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 0.19% today to close at $422.78, continuing a strong two-week rally that's now up 9.05%. The move reflects an environment where US oil has climbed to $107 a barrel amid Middle East tensions—a Saudi pipeline closure and Houthi attacks have created genuine supply concerns—while US refineries are running at 96.8% capacity, meaning tight supply conditions benefit refining margins. The company benefits directly when crude prices are elevated and refineries operate at high utilization rates, both of which are currently in place.

The broader backdrop matters: record diesel prices are beginning to ripple through transportation costs across the economy, which typically supports sustained energy demand and refining spreads. Diesel and heating oil storage sits at 107.9 million barrels—relatively low—which further supports the case for refinery operations to stay strong in the near term.
